channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
item.description: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.

item.title: [DW] Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with the UK monarch and relatively new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

item.title: [DW] EU summons Russian envoy over failed Leipzig drone attack
item.description: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the attempted attack had "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism." She said the EU was summoning a Russian envoy, with France announcing a similar step.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU moves to curb Airbnb‑style rentals in bid to ease housing stress
item.description: The EU's Affordable housing act lays out a comprehensive plan to curb tourist rentals, while giving power back to local regions. But is it doing enough?

item.title: [EU Observer] Ceuta’s migration crisis is becoming a gift to Spain’s (and Europe’s) far-right
item.description: Ceuta’s migration crisis is putting Spain and the EU under growing pressure. With little concrete support from Brussels and conditions still tough on the ground, frustrations are rising — and Spain’s far-right Vox is making the most of it ahead of the 2027 elections.

item.title: [EU Observer] Top Russian oligarch Abramovich loses third EU lawsuit, as Brussels plans tougher blacklist
item.description: If the EU wanted some red meat in its next sanctions, there were plenty of billionaires left to bite who, like Abramovich, "generate significant revenues for the Russian government".

item.title: [EU Observer] EU promises to look beyond ‘price alone’ in reform of public procurement rules
item.description: The European Commission says that new public procurement rules would allow more flexibility in choosing the best offer, stopping the "race to the bottom" for the lowest bid.

item.title: [ECFR] A future with Chinese characteristics
item.description: The world is undergoing a historical and cultural rupture. Just as Hollywood and other American exports once gave the rest of the world a glimpse of modern life and the future that awaited them, China is now doing the same for African, Latin American and even American young people

item.title: [ECFR] Friends without benefits: Why the EU should offer Canada more than casual defence ties
item.description: Trump is pushing Canada—a quiet military powerhouse—away from America. The EU should seize the chance and fold it into its own defence

item.title: [DW] German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
item.description: The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm.

item.title: [DW] Ratko Mladic’s funeral casts shadow over Bosnia and Herzegovina vote
item.description: Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, has deepened regional tensions and could affect the upcoming election in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

item.title: [ECFR] Future nostalgia: Europe’s unfinished song
item.description: ECFR’s new research reveals Europeans are suffering from an imagination gap. Many people want to see Europe strong and flourishing—but fewer can picture a credible route from today’s disruptions to that destination

item.title: [ECFR] Beyond Saxony-Anhalt: What Merz’s crisis means for Europe
item.description: The far-right AfD’s win in a small German state calls for dynamism in Berlin and hedging in Brussels

item.title: [ECFR] Emergency Room: The AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Jana Puglierin, senior policy fellow and head of ECFR’s Berlin office, to discuss the Alternative for Germany (AfD)’s election win in Saxony-Anhalt—and what it means for Germany and Europe

item.title: [ECFR] Britons back ban on trade with Israeli settlements by more than two to one
item.description: New polling published by ECFR shows that Britons across the political divide favour banning trade with illegal Israeli settlements

item.title: [DW] Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
item.description: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to pay Naftogaz damages.

item.title: [Financial Times] Oracle’s data centre revenue surges as AI strategy accelerates
item.description: Faster sales growth suggests progress in its risky push to compete in the AI infrastructure race

item.title: [Financial Times] Anthropic says it stopped scientists potentially developing bioweapons with AI
item.description: Start-up discloses five examples of when users ‘circumvented controls’ and made efforts to ‘obfuscate’ the purpose of their research

item.title: [Financial Times] Global bond sell-off reignites as oil jumps to $109
item.description: US yields reach highs of the day after Scott Bessent’s Treasury buyback operation undershoots its target

item.title: [Politico Europe] Tusk warns of future attacks after ‘direct threat’ averted at Poland-Ukraine border
item.description: Polish prime minister spoke of U.S. intel pointing to various scenarios, not just on the Russia-Ukraine border but the whole Eastern flank.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Kazakhstan can’t sing its way into Eurovision in 2027
item.description: The EBU says the country “does not qualify for full membership at this time.”

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘She killed me with her post’: Gaza students caught in Belgium minister’s immigration posturing
item.description: Belgium's immigration minister has gone on the warpath against evacuating 13 students from Gaza, but they might still be flying out despite her anti-Arab and pro-Israel dog-whistling.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez invited to Paris for Gabriel Zucman’s tax-the-rich summit
item.description: The economist's big event comes shortly after the launch of his new book.

item.title: [Financial Times] How would Trump’s $5,000 voting payout work?
item.description: President’s pledge to give cash to all American adults if Republicans win midterms will be at heart of his party’s campaign

item.title: [Politico Europe] Bad actors in China and Russia are already weaponizing Anthropic’s AI
item.description: Anthropic says foreign scientists, hackers and security services circumvented restrictions to use Claude for dangerous work, including possible bioweapons research.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Macron’s space summit showed Europe isn’t ready for takeoff without the US
item.description: The two-day gathering in Paris left some participants disappointed.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine’s financial crisis resurrects Europe’s bitter dilemma on Russian frozen assets
item.description: The dire financial situation of Ukraine, ahead of what is expected to be a difficult winter with a possible further Russian mobilisation, has reopened the discussion on whether to use Russian frozen assets — raising difficult questions over legality, financial stability and Europe’s leverage in any future peace deal.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU prosecutors should go after sanctions busters, top diplomat suggests
item.description: Kaja Kallas wants the European Public Prosecutor’s Office to be given a mandate to squeeze Russia's war machine.

item.title: [Financial Times] Druckenmiller says US borrowing costs still ‘a little low’ despite surge in yields
item.description: Close ally of Kevin Warsh says Federal Reserve officials who argue rates are restrictive are ‘just ridiculous’

item.title: [Politico Europe] Le Pen-Bardella, tandem en péril ?
item.description: Très attendu par ses troupes, le premier discours de Marine Le Pen en tant que candidate officielle du RN à la présidentielle, dimanche à Hénin-Beaumont, va-t-il dissiper les interrogations nées de la rentrée mouvementée du Rassemblement national ? La reprise en main de la députée va-t-elle entraîner la mise à l’écart de Jordan Bardella, le […]

item.title: [DW] Germany’s Goethe-Institut is closing in Russia. Russians tell DW how canceled exams are upending their plans
item.description: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia affects their lives.

item.title: [Financial Times] Vantage Data Centers seeks $2bn in loans from Pimco and PGIM
item.description: DigitalBridge-backed firm taps new investors for AI infrastructure as Wall Street banks limit exposure

item.title: [Politico Europe] Farage donor scandal turns spotlight on UK polling industry
item.description: Former employees and clients of JL Partners say there have been other instances of funders not being declared.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU asylum claims drop to lowest level in five years, but many still lost at sea
item.description: Despite increased calls to curb migration, asylum application numbers have been following a downward trend, due to geopolitical circumstances and EU cooperation with third countries. Migrants deaths on the journey, however, are far from dropping.

item.title: [EU Observer] Cleared in Greek border case, Austrian activist now sues EU data chief over Europol record
item.description: An Austrian national who helped document rights violations at the Greek Turkey border in 2020 is suing the EU's data protection watchdog over allegations it failed to protect her rights after Europol collected her personal information amid a Greek criminal case, for which she was later exonerated.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Lagarde rejects far-left Mélenchon’s debt-cancellation plan
item.description: French presidential candidate renewed his call in August for the ECB to freeze pandemic-era government debt.

item.title: [EU Observer] ECB raises rates again as Strait of Hormuz disruption drives up gas prices
item.description: The conflict in the Middle East has pushed up energy-related inflation by 14.3 percent year-on-year

item.title: [Politico Europe] Lagarde brushes off exit gossip as ECB raises rates
item.description: ECB president has floated early ECB departure to play a role in the French presidential campaign.

item.title: [Financial Times] Houthis capture Red Sea port in blow to Saudis
item.description: Rebels overrun historic Yemeni port of Mocha as they advance south towards strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait

item.title: [EU Observer] EU moves to expand ‘outermost region’ privileges as Spain presses Ceuta and Melilla claim
item.description: The EU Commission says its 'omnibus' bill published on Thursday (10 September), will build on the special legal status that the so-called 'outermost regions' of the 27-member bloc have.

item.title: [EU Observer] Putin spent over €110bn on Ukraine war so far in 2026, up one-third on last year (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,659)
item.description: New budget data and battlefield videos reveal a Russia quietly scrambling to finance soaring war costs, hide territorial setbacks and defend supposedly “safe” assets thousands of kilometres from the front.

item.title: [DW] Are electric vehicles really bad for the environment?
item.description: Some German politicians are calling for a delay to the EU plan to phase out gas-powered vehicles, saying cars must be judged on the entire carbon footprint. But the full picture still says EVs are more climate friendly.

item.title: [Financial Times] Hugging Face co-founder: What we learnt from OpenAI’s hack
item.description: Commercial AI tools failed to defend the platform against the attack — the solution lies in open-weight models

item.title: [ECFR] Booted, then suited: Veterans and the making of Putin’s new proto-elite
item.description: The Kremlin is promoting Ukraine war veterans--cultivating a proto-elite who could reinforce Russia’s militarised course.

item.title: [Financial Times] Saudi Arabia cuts oil output to lowest this year on Houthi threats
item.description: Rebels announced ‘maritime embargo’ against kingdom’s exports in July, forcing world’s biggest exporter to cut production

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen’s State of the Union AI data-centre dream will be a nightmare
item.description: As Ursula von der Leyen gears up to talk up her data centre plans in the State of the Union address next Wednesday (16 September), MEPs must question who will own and benefit from these data centres.

item.title: [EU Observer] Finland’s first licence to mine a Natura 2000 site would set a deadly precedent for EU nature protection
item.description: The Viiankiaapa peat bog in Finland faces permanent destruction for a short-term mining project. Even more worryingly, this could be a dangerous test case for the interests of mining for minerals overriding the public interest to preserve nature.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: why are European students falling behind?
item.description: The 2025 PISA results were published a few days ago. And they’re quite a bad surprise for most European countries. Educational performance is declining almost everywhere on the continent.

item.title: [EU Observer] Chinese Mission to the EU holds China-EU table tennis friendship tournament
item.description: Last weekend, the Mission of China to the EU and the Euroclub jointly hosted the China-EU Table Tennis Friendship Tournament in Brussels. More than 100 table tennis enthusiasts from China, the European institutions and the European Parliament participated in the event.

item.title: [DW] Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
item.description: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump promises $5,000 ‘dividend’ for US voters if Republicans win midterms
item.description: President puts himself at centre of congressional election campaign despite his plummeting approval ratings

item.title: [Financial Times] Silicon Valley bets on the impossible again
item.description: Tech investors are rediscovering the kind of long-shot sci-fi bets that helped build Silicon Valley

item.title: [Financial Times] Starbucks bets $1bn on coffee house antidote to lonely digital lives
item.description: Easy chairs and rugs are part of chief executive Brian Niccol’s plan to make shops more inviting and boost sales

item.title: [DW] US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

item.title: [DW] Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
item.description: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

item.title: [DW] Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions
item.description: Hungary's new prime minister promised he would recover billions stolen or diverted by the previous administration. A new "super authority" is about to begin that work. Its success or failure will have a big impact.

item.title: [DW] War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
item.description: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.

item.title: [ECFR] Climate of concern: The changing face of social movements in North Africa
item.description: Social movements in North Africa increasingly focus on environmental concerns and the impact of climate change. Europeans must ensure their cooperation with governments in the region does not end up adding to activists’ grievances

item.title: [ECFR] After Tidö: What a centre-left Sweden would change for Europe
item.description: Magdalena Andersson of the Social Democrats is the favourite to become Sweden's next prime minister, but only after months of hard coalition bargaining. Who she governs with would shape how far her foreign policy shifts

item.title: [ECFR] Actually, maybe: How German Angst could become Europe’s nightmare
item.description: Germany’s political centre is crumbling—but its leaders appear unable to get ahead of the impending crisis

item.title: [ECFR] Against war, drought and hunger: A global coalition to prevent a food crisis
item.description: Three features of today’s unordered world are converging to create a devastating food crisis. Russia’s war in Ukraine is disrupting agricultural exports from both countries. The enduring blockage of the Strait of Hormuz is restricting fertiliser shipments. And this year’s El Niño (a sporadic warming of the Pacific Ocean generating widespread knock-on effects elsewhere) could […]

item.title: [DW] Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
item.description: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: How the funeral of Ratko Mladic is dividing a nation
item.description: As the Serbian government leaves the decision about Ratko Mladic's funeral arrangements to his family, international pressure on the country is mounting. How do Serbs feel about the matter?

item.title: [ECFR] Orchestrators, not customers: A new role for European governments in defence
item.description: Weapons that took decades to develop can now be countered within months. European governments need to stop buying finished platforms and start running an innovation cycle, in which soldiers learn from one system and build these lessons into the next

item.title: [ECFR] Bonus episode: The EU enlargement game
item.description: In a special episode recorded live from Lisbon, Jessica Hendrick puts six EU candidate countries through an enlargement simulation to find out what happens when crisis, cash, disinformation and political pressure collide with the race to join the EU

item.title: [ECFR] A no to the EU, not to Europe: What Icelanders actually voted on
item.description: Icelanders voted no because of old, domestic reasons: fish, the currency and comfort with the status quo. The result was not a victory for the far-right—but the heated campaign is a warning sign for Icelandic political life.

item.title: [ECFR] Maximum pressure on Iran, round two
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Ellie Geranmayeh to discuss the latest phase of the US-Iran conflict, the escalating economic pressure campaign against Tehran and the risks of a prolonged war without a clear exit strategy
